The story does not have a balance between the two elements; instead, it relies almost exclusively on 'scene'. Written in the format of a dramatic script, the entire narrative unfolds in real-time through dialogue and brief stage directions (character interactions and actions). There is no narrative 'summary' to compress time, nor is there direct 'exposition' to explain the characters' shared history (such as who Katrin is, the significance of the watch, or what the spring message said)—all background information is merely hinted at through the immediate conversation.
